findings.reason: a node implementing "skip any review that lists an absent item" silently re-reviews 51 plans whose design reviews were complete when written, and the section must state that census and decide (grandfather the item the rubric gained, or accept the re-review) as §14 did for its own sidecar census, or scope the skip to the content rubric.
findings.text: the deliverable says a delivered review whose `absent_items` is not empty "covers no unit", as though the only such review were §40's incident; a census of `docs/state/reckon/reviews/plan/**/*.json` (1388 stored plan reviews) finds 122 with a non-empty `absent_items`, of which exactly 1 is the content review of `budget-fits-a-worker-window` (`['anchors_resolve']`, the incident) and 121 are design reviews across 51 distinct plans, every one carrying `absent_items: ['interface_budget']` and every one written before 2026-10-05, when §13 added `interface_budget` as the fifth design item — so their `absent_items` records a rubric that grew after the review was written, not an unread review; a design review contributes coverage (routing.py:2557, "a design review also covers the content it read"), and `newest_design_review` (plan_review.py:1179) is consulted for presence alone, so the skip would stop those 121 reviews covering and flip their plans to uncovered.

findings.reason: the case must also store a design review, or assert that the refusal names the uncovered units, or it passes for a reason unrelated to the fix.
findings.text: the second case, "a plan whose only stored review is missing one rubric item reads as uncovered through `review_coverage`, and `require_plan_reviewed` refuses a dispatch on it", cannot exercise the coverage predicate as worded: `require_plan_reviewed` refuses before it calls `review_coverage` when the plan carries no stored design review (`newest_design_review` returns None at routing.py:2554-2571, and the refusal names the design rubric), so a plan holding one absent-item content review and nothing else is refused for the design reason and the case proves nothing about the coverage predicate.

findings.reason: the plan should say whether the bullet tolerance covers the health grammar (which its tests do), or direct the plan-report parser to its own unshared pattern, so a node does not change an unrelated grammar with no test.
findings.text: the deliverable says "both line patterns read a ... line that a Markdown list marker introduces", but `_PLAN_RUBRIC_LINE_RE` (review.py:1249) is shared with the health-review grammar: `_opens_health_record` (review.py:1443) and `parse_health_review` (review.py:1585) both read it, while the health grammar reads its findings through the separate `_HEALTH_FINDING_LINE_RE` (review.py:1369), so widening the shared pattern to accept `- `, `* ` or `1. ` also widens the health-review record opener and its RUBRIC lines while leaving its FINDING lines anchored — an untested change to a grammar the section never mentions.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves: `reckon/crew/review.py` "near line 1249" is `_PLAN_RUBRIC_LINE_RE` at :1249, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` "near line 211" is `DEFAULT_STATUS` at :211, "near line 797" is `review_coverage` at :797, and `reckon/crew/routing.py` "near line 2489" is `require_plan_reviewed` at :2489.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the gate case as worded cannot reach the coverage predicate it exists to test, and no case measures the population the new skip flips.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the arms and the fragment log sit under the run directory and `docs/evidence/fragments/...`, not a scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the test filename, the symbols or the evidence path.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the skip's blast radius is 121 stored design reviews across 51 plans, none named by the section's evidence and none measured by its done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the two halves (read a bulleted line; cover no unit when an item is absent) serve one verdict, that a delivered review is read whole, and each carries its own assertion and its own control.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s40 declares no depends-on, and none is needed: its write paths (`reckon/crew/review.py`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, the new test) are disjoint from §37/§38/§39, and the receipt field it references is explicitly §37's rather than a dependency.
